answer: Persistent Neighbor Ledger. Each agent records its ten most frequent counterparties; a new identity must appear in several existing ledgers before routing through the lantern hub. The wharf gateway only forwards traffic whose counterparties form a closed, mutually observed neighborhood, checked against ledger history. Faking that costs an attacker sustained real volume with many distinct agents, plus timber spent maintaining those links over time—roughly weeks of genuine trade per identity.
